questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
An automobile retailer had an adult daughter who needed a car in her employment but had only $3,000 with which to buy one. The retailer wrote to her, "Give me your $3,000 and I'll give you the car on our lot that we have been using as a demonstrator." The daughter thanked her father and paid him the $3,000. As both the retailer and the daughter knew, the demonstrator was reasonably worth $10,000. After the daughter paid the $3,000, but before the car was delivered to her, one of the retailer's sales staff sold and delivered the same car to a customer for $10,000. Neither the salesperson nor the customer was aware of the transaction between the retailer and the daughter.
Does the daughter, after rejecting a tendered return of the $3,000 by the retailer, have an action against him for breach of contract?

choices.A: No, because the payment of $3,000 was inadequate consideration to support the retailer's promise.
choices.B: No, because the salesperson's delivery of the car to the customer made it impossible for the retailer to perform.
choices.C: Yes, because the retailer's promise was supported by bargained-for consideration.
choices.D: Yes, because the retailer's promise was supported by the moral obligation a father owes his child as to the necessities of modern life.

questions.explanation:
Elements of valuable consideration
Bargained-for exchange Each party's willingness to enter agreement must be induced by other party's act/promise
Legal detriment Each party must relinquish legal right by either:
  • performing (or promising to perform) act that is not legally required or
  • refraining (or promising to refrain) from performing legally permissible act

A valid contract is formed when a mutual agreement is supported by adequate consideration—ie, a bargained-for exchange of promises or performance. If the exchange involves items with economic value (eg, a car in exchange for money), there is no additional requirement that their values be equivalent or even roughly equivalent.

Here, the retailer promised to give the daughter the demonstrator car in exchange for $3,000. Although the car was worth $10,000, this difference in value did not prevent the daughter's payment from being consideration for the retailer's promise (Choice A). Therefore, a valid contract arose between the parties, and the daughter has a breach of contract action against the retailer.

(Choice B) A party's contractual duties may be discharged if it has become objectively impossible to perform them. But impossibility does not apply when, as here, a seller or its agent sells contracted-for goods to someone else.

(Choice D) A promise based on a moral obligation is not supported by consideration and will not give rise to a contract. In addition, parents have no obligation—moral or otherwise—to provide their adult child with a car.

📌 Educational Objective

A difference in economic value between the items exchanged is not ground for finding that a contract did not exist due to inadequate consideration.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 71 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (bargained-for exchange requirement).
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 79 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (adequacy of consideration).
questions.zh-question:
一位汽车零售商有一个成年女儿，因工作需要一辆车，但她只有3000美元可以用来买车。该零售商写信给她说：“把你那3000美元给我，我就把我们车场里一直用作展示车的那辆车给你。”女儿感谢了她的父亲，并支付给他3000美元。零售商和女儿都知道，这辆展示车的合理价值为10000美元。在女儿支付了3000美元之后，但在车交付给她之前，该零售商的一名销售人员以10000美元的价格将同一辆车出售并交付给了一位顾客。销售人员和顾客都不知道零售商与女儿之间的这笔交易。

在女儿拒绝了零售商提出的退还3000美元的提议后，她是否可以以违约为由对其提起诉讼？

zh-choices.A: 不可以，因为支付3000美元不足以构成支持零售商承诺的对价。
zh-choices.B: 不可以，因为销售人员将车交付给顾客，使得零售商无法履行合同。
zh-choices.C: 可以，因为零售商的承诺有经协商议价的对价作为支持。
zh-choices.D: 可以，因为零售商的承诺有父亲对子女在现代生活必需品方面所负的道德义务作为支持。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Formation of Contracts - Formation of Contracts

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：讨价还价交换（bargained-for exchange）是否成立；就算车值 $10,000、只付 $3,000，价差也不影响有无对价。

三秒认题路径：

承诺换钱 → 双方都想交换 → 价值不等也行 → 仍有对价 → 可起诉违约

核心法律规则

抓住这条规则就够了

对价（consideration）看的是有没有讨价还价交换（bargained-for exchange），不是两边值不值一样多；只要一方的给付是为了换另一方的承诺，就够了。

法律损害（legal detriment）的考场意思：一方放弃了本来可以不做的事，或者做了本来没义务做的事，就能构成对价。

所以，这里女儿交 $3,000 是在换父亲/零售商给那辆展车；价值不对等（inadequate consideration）不会自动把合同打掉。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 71、§ 79 - 只要是交换，不要求经济价值相等。

思维导图

题眼：3,000 换展车，车值 10,000，但女儿已经付款
先看：是不是讨价还价交换（bargained-for exchange）？
是：女儿付款是为了拿车，商家承诺是为了拿钱。
再看：钱和车不必等价；价差不是无对价。
结论：合同成立 → 先卖给别人构成违约 → 选 C。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：车明明值 $10,000，女儿只付 $3,000，好像“太便宜”，所以没有真正的交换。

但考试真正问的是：双方有没有拿各自的承诺来换对方的给付，不是法官觉得划不划算。

司法考试看的是「有没有法律上的交换」，而不是「双方经济上是否对等」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干的$3,000 换展车就是标准交换；对价（consideration）已成立，所以零售商把车卖给别人后，女儿能告违约。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把价差当成无对价，错把“便宜”理解成“没交换”。

❌ 法律适用 | 不履行归责误判

✕ B: 把卖给第三人硬套成impossible to perform，其实是自己先违约，不是不能履行。

❌ 事实误判 | 道德义务偷换

✕ D: 硬把父女关系塞进moral obligation，但成人子女买车没有这种对价基础。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓“有没有交换”，再看“价差是否重要”；只要是 bargain，就别被金额大小带偏。

考场速记

记忆口诀：“有交换就有对价，价钱不等也照样成立。” 看到 bargained-for exchange 先想有没有“拿一个换另一个”，不要先算公平不公平。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
An employer encourages "wellness" on the part of his employees and supports various physical fitness programs to that end. Learning that one of his employees was a dedicated jogger, the employer promised to pay her a special award of $100 if she were to run one mile in less than six minutes on the following Saturday. The employee thanked him and did in fact run a mile in less than six minutes on the day specified. Shortly thereafter, however, the employer discovered that for more than a year the employee had been running at least one mile in less than six minutes every day as part of her personal fitness program. He then refused to pay the $100.
In an action by the employee against the employer for breach of contract, which of the following best summarizes the probable decision of the court?

choices.A: The employee wins, because running a mile in less than six minutes is a significantly demanding enterprise.
choices.B: The employee wins, because she ran the specified mile as requested, and her motives for doing so are irrelevant.
choices.C: The employer wins, because it is a compelling inference that his promise did not induce the employee to run the specified mile.
choices.D: The employer wins, because the employee's running of the specified mile was beneficial, not detrimental, to her in any event.

questions.explanation:
Elements of valuable consideration
Bargained-for exchange Each party's willingness to enter agreement must be induced by other party's act/promise
Legal detriment Each party must relinquish legal right by either:
  • performing (or promising to perform) act that is not legally required or
  • refraining (or promising to refrain) from performing legally permissible act

Forming a valid contract requires consideration—ie, a bargained-for exchange of promises or performance. This requires each party to:

  • perform or promise to perform some act that is not legally required or
  • refrain or promise to refrain from performing some legally permissible act.

Here, the employer promised to pay the employee $100 if she were to run a mile in less than six minutes on the following Saturday, and the employee ran the mile as requested. This exchange (employer's promise for employee's performance) provided the necessary consideration to form a binding contract—regardless of the employee's motives for running the mile. Therefore, the court should decide that the employee wins.

(Choice A) The fact that running a mile in less than six minutes is a significantly demanding enterprise is irrelevant to determining whether bargained-for consideration exists.

(Choice C) Although the employee runs at least one mile in less than six minutes every day, this does not give rise to an inference that the employer's promise did not induce her to run the specified mile.

(Choice D) The employee suffered a legal detriment (as is required for consideration) by running the specified mile because she was not legally required to perform this act.

📌 Educational Objective

Contracts must be supported by consideration—ie, a bargained-for exchange of promises or performance—which requires each party to (1) perform or promise to perform an act that is not legally required or (2) refrain or promise to refrain from performing some legally permissible act.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 71 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (bargained-for exchange as consideration).

一名雇主鼓励其员工保持“健康”，并为此支持各种体育健身项目。在得知他的一名员工是慢跑爱好者后，该雇主承诺，如果她在下周六能于六分钟内跑完一英里，就付给她100美元的特别奖励。该员工向他表示感谢，并确实在指定的日期以不到六分钟的时间跑完了一英里。然而，此后不久，雇主发现该员工在过去一年多的时间里，每天都会在六分钟内跑完至少一英里，作为她个人健身计划的一部分。于是，他拒绝支付这100美元。

在该员工以违约为由对雇主提起的诉讼中，以下哪项最能概括法院可能作出的判决？

zh-choices.A: 员工胜诉，因为在六分钟内跑完一英里是一项要求很高的任务。
zh-choices.B: 员工胜诉，因为她按要求跑完了指定的一英里，而她这样做的动机无关紧要。
zh-choices.C: 雇主胜诉，因为可以有力地推断，他的承诺并未诱使员工跑完指定的一英里。
zh-choices.D: 雇主胜诉，因为无论如何，员工跑完指定的一英里对她是有益而非有害的。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Formation of Contracts - Consideration

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：对价（consideration）里的 约定交换（bargained-for exchange），以及“动机是不是必须认真看”。

三秒认题路径：

老板许诺 $100 → 员工照做 → 看是否诱发交换 → 不看主观动机 → 选员工赢

核心法律规则

合同要成立，必须有 对价（consideration），也就是一方的承诺或履行，诱发 了另一方的承诺或履行。考场意思：不是看这件事难不难、值不值，而是看双方是不是在做“你给我、我给你”的交换。

法律损害（legal detriment） 只要求一方去做本来没法律义务做的事，或者不去做本来可以做的事。考场意思：员工按要求跑完这一英里，就已经交出了对价；她以前天天跑，不会自动把这次交换变没。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 71：只要承诺与履行构成约定交换，动机是否“顺手”“顺便”通常不影响对价成立。

思维导图

1. 雇主的条件
“跑进 6 分钟以内”才给钱，这就是交换条件。
2. 员工的履行
她按要求完成了指定一英里，满足了承诺对应的行为。
3. 交换是否成立
题干要看的是是否 诱发承诺，不是她心里想什么。
4. 干扰点
她平时也跑得很快，只是“背景事实”，不否定这次 bargained-for exchange。
5. 结论
有对价，就有合同；员工完成条件，所以她赢。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：她本来就天天跑，而且跑得很轻松，所以老板的承诺好像没“换来”什么新东西。

但考试真正问的是：这次承诺有没有换来她按指定条件去做事，而不是她平时是不是也会跑。

题目看的是“有没有约定交换”，不是“这件事对她有没有压力”。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干 老板先许诺、员工后完成指定跑步，已经形成 约定交换（bargained-for exchange）；她为什么去跑，不影响对价成立。

❌ 概念混淆 | 难度当对价

✕ A: 把 significantly demanding 当成门槛了，难不难不是对价标准。

❌ 事实误判 | 动机偷换

✕ C: 她平时也跑得快，只能说明背景习惯，不能推翻这次承诺诱发了履行。

❌ 法律适用 | 负担标准错位

✕ D: beneficial 不会否定对价；题目要看是否放弃了法律上可不做的事。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓“承诺是否换来履行”，再看有没有被题干里的背景习惯带偏。

考场速记

记忆口诀：对价看交换，不看动机；只要承诺换来了履行，通常就够了。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
On June 1, a wholesaler received a purchase-order form from a retailer that was a new customer, in which the retailer ordered 1,000 anti-recoil widgets for delivery no later than August 30 at a delivered total price of $10,000, as quoted in the wholesaler's current catalog. Both parties are merchants with respect to widgets of all types. On June 2, the wholesaler mailed to the retailer its own form, across the top of which the wholesaler's president had written, "We are pleased to accept your order." This form contained the same terms as the retailer's form except for an additional printed clause in the wholesaler's form that provided for a maximum liability of $100 for any breach of contract by the wholesaler.
As of June 5, when the retailer received the wholesaler's acceptance form, which of the following is an accurate statement concerning the legal relationship between the retailer and wholesaler?

choices.A: There is an enforceable contract whose terms do not include the liability-limitation clause in the wholesaler's form.
choices.B: There is an enforceable contract whose terms include the liability-limitation clause in the wholesaler's form, because liquidation of damages is expressly authorized by the Uniform Commercial Code.
choices.C: There is no contract, because the liability-limitation clause in the wholesaler's form is a material alteration of the retailer's offer.
choices.D: There is no contract, because the retailer did not consent to the liability-limitation clause in the wholesaler's form.

questions.explanation:
Effect of new terms in reply to offer
Common law
(mirror-image)
  • Offer rejected
  • Reply treated as counteroffer
UCC
(battle of the forms) 		≥1 party is
nonmerchant
  • Offer accepted unless reply expressly required assent to new/revised terms
  • New/revised terms treated as proposed additions to contract
All parties are
merchants
  • Offer accepted unless reply expressly required assent to new/revised terms
  • New terms become part of contract unless:
    • offer expressly required assent to new terms
    • new terms materially alter contract or
    • offeror objects within reasonable time
  • Revised terms follow split authority & are either:
    • treated as new terms or
    • cancelled out under knockout rule
UCC = Uniform Commercial Code.

Contracts for the sale of goods are governed by Article 2 of the Uniform Commercial Code (UCC), which follows the battle-of-the-forms rule for contract formation. Under this rule, an enforceable contract is created once there has been an offer and a reasonable manifestation of acceptance (even one that includes new terms). But in a contract between merchants, the new terms will fall away—ie, will not become part of the contract—if:

  • the offer expressly required assent to new terms (and the offeror does not assent)
  • the offeror objects within a reasonable time or
  • the new terms materially alter the contract (eg, change a party's risks or remedies).

Here, the retailer sent a purchase order for 1,000 widgets. The wholesaler then mailed an acceptance form, which created an enforceable contract despite containing an additional clause limiting the wholesaler's liability for breach to $100 ((Choice C)). The retailer's order (ie, offer) did not expressly require consent to new terms, and the retailer did not object to the new term. But since the new term materially alters the contract by limiting the retailer's remedy for breach, the contract does not include the liability-limitation clause.

(Choice B) The UCC expressly authorizes liquidation of damages—ie, contractually stipulating to a reasonable estimate of the actual damages to be recovered if one party breaches. But $100 is not a reasonable estimate for a $10,000 sales contract. And even if it were, the new liability-limitation clause still materially alters the contract.

(Choice D) Had the retailer's offer expressly required assent to new terms, the retailer's failure to consent would prevent the new term from becoming part of the contract. But it would not prevent contract formation.

📌 Educational Objective

Under the UCC's battle-of-the-forms rule, an acceptance is effective even if it contains new terms. But in a contract between merchants, the new terms fall away if (1) the offer expressly required assent to new terms and no assent was given, (2) the offeror objects within a reasonable time, or (3) the new terms materially alter the contract.

📚 References
  • U.C.C. § 2-207 (Am. Law Inst. & Unif. Law Comm'n 2019) (battle-of-the-forms rule).

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Formation of Contracts - Mutual assent

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：UCC 第2-207条（battle of the forms）里，卖方回函虽然加了新条款，但合同先成立，新增的责任限制条款不一定自动进合同。

三秒认题路径：

货物买卖 → 双方商人 → 回函加新条款 → 先成约后审条款 → 看是否落空

核心法律规则

要约（offer）加上有效承诺（acceptance），合同（contract）就先成立；在货物买卖里，UCC允许承诺里带新条款，不会因为“不是镜像”就直接把合同打掉。

但如果双方都是商人，新条款只有在没有被要约明确要求同意、没有及时反对、而且不属于会实质性改变（materially alter）合同的内容时，才可能进入合同；像限制卖方违约责任的条款，考试里通常就是会把买方坑小一圈的典型陷阱。

核心判例： U.C.C. § 2-207 直接锁定结论：回函仍可成约，但新增的责任限制条款要过商人之间的“落入合同”审查。

思维导图

先看：卖方回函有没有先让合同成立？
YES：采购单已是要约，回函写“accept”就是承诺，contract formed。
再看新增条款能不能进合同：
卡死点：liability-limitation clause 会改变救济，通常属 materially alter。
结果：新条款掉出去，正确答案到 A。
NO：只有在回函根本不是承诺时，才会走到“无合同”；本题不是这个路。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：卖方一加新条款，买方没点头，那就没有合同。

但考试真正问的是：合同先不先成立，和新条款能不能留下来，是两步题。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干里卖方已写明接受，合同先成立；但liability-limitation clause 会实质性改变救济，所以这条新内容不进合同。

❌ 法律适用 | 液化损害误判

✕ B: 把liquidation of damages当成免责万能条，忽略了这里是责任限制条款。

❌ 概念混淆 | 镜像规则误判

✕ C: 误把商人间回函当普通法镜像承诺，看到新条款就直接判“没合同”。

❌ 事实误判 | 同意缺失偷换

✕ D: 题干没说买方要求逐项同意，命题人想骗你把“没同意新条款”偷换成“没成约”。

这题建议用什么方法？

先判合同是否成立，再单独审查新条款能不能留在合同里。

考场速记

记住一句：UCC 2-207 先保合同、后筛条款；商人之间的回函加新项，不等于合同没了。

遇到考试里的“新条款能不能进合同”，先问三件事：有没有明确要求同意、有没有及时反对、是不是 materially alter。本题的答案就是：合同有，新增责任限制条款没有。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
A producer of small engines contracted to supply 5,000 engines per month of a specified model to a lawn mower manufacturer for the next three years at an agreed-upon price. The producer sent the manufacturer a form quotation that included a standard "boilerplate" indemnification clause requiring the manufacturer to indemnify the producer for losses arising from the transaction. The producer's form also included a statute-of-limitations provision requiring that claims arising from defective engines be brought within one year of delivery.
The manufacturer subsequently ordered engines using a form requiring the producer to indemnify the manufacturer for any loss arising from engine defects and specifying a three-year statute of limitations for claims arising from the engines.
Two years later, the manufacturer discovered that 20% of the engines delivered in the first year were defective and filed suit against the producer seeking indemnification. The jurisdiction has adopted the Uniform Commercial Code (UCC) gap-filling provisions, which include a default four-year statute of limitations.
Is the manufacturer likely to prevail in its suit against the producer for losses arising from the defective engines?

choices.A: No, because a contract is only enforceable under the mirror-image rule if there is a meeting of the minds on all terms.
choices.B: No, because the producer is master of the offer and therefore the contractual terms in its form quotation control.
choices.C: Yes, because the producer failed to object to the conflicting terms when it accepted the manufacturer's purchase order.
choices.D: Yes, because the UCC operates to replace the conflicting statutes of limitations with its four-year statute of limitations.

questions.explanation:
Effect of revised term on contract formation
Mirror-image
(common law)

"I will give you $500 to paint my porch on June 1."
Acceptance
"I will paint your porch on June 1 for $300."
No contract
Battle of the forms
(UCC)
All merchants

1. 1000 widgets
2. $5 each
3. Delivery June 1
Buyer's form
1. 1000 widgets
2. $3 each
3. Delivery June 1
"Knock out" & use gap-filler
2. $5 each 2. $3 each

≥ 1 nonmerchant
Seller's form
1. 1000 widgets
2. $5 each
3. Delivery June 1
Buyer's form
1. 1000 widgets
2. $3 each
3. Delivery June 1
Proposed additions
2. $5 each 2. $3 each
Contract formed
UCC = Uniform Commercial Code

Contracts for the sale of goods (eg, engines) are governed by the UCC. Under the UCC's battle-of-the-forms rule for contract formation, an acceptance is effective even if it contains revised (ie, conflicting) terms that are different from the offer. In contracts between merchants, the revised terms are canceled out by the knockout rule (adopted in most jurisdictions). When gaps are created after applying the knockout rule, the court uses the UCC's gap-filling provisions to patch the holes.

Here, the manufacturer brought suit after two years. The producer's form quotation (offer) had specified a one-year statute of limitations for defective-engine claims, while the manufacturer's order form (acceptance) specified a three-year statute of limitations. Both parties are merchants, so the conflicting statute-of-limitations terms are canceled out by the knockout rule. Since the UCC operates to replace those terms with its four-year statute of limitations, the manufacturer is likely to prevail.

(Choice A) Under the common law mirror-image rule, an acceptance must mirror the terms of the offer. A purported acceptance that includes revised or new terms is treated as both a rejection of the original offer and a counteroffer. But since this rule only applies to services and real estate contracts, it does not apply here.

(Choice B) The offeror, as master of the offer, can dictate the manner and means of acceptance. Here, however, the producer's (offeror's) form quotation did not require the manufacturer to accept the one-year statute of limitations provision for an acceptance to be effective.

(Choice C) A few jurisdictions do not follow the knockout rule and instead treat a revised term in an acceptance as a "new" term. New terms are automatically included in a contract between merchants unless, inter alia,* the offeror objects within a reasonable time. But this minority rule does not apply here.

*Other exceptions to the automatic inclusion of new terms arise when (1) the term materially alters the original contract or (2) the offer expressly limited acceptance to its terms.

📌 Educational Objective

In contracts between merchants, revised (ie, conflicting) terms in the offer and acceptance are canceled out under the knockout rule and replaced with UCC gap-filling provisions.

📚 References
  • U.C.C. § 2-207 (Am. Law Inst. & Unif. Law Comm'n 2020) (new terms in acceptance or confirmation).
  • U.C.C. § 2-725 (Am. Law Inst. & Unif. Law Comm'n 2020) (statute of limitations in contracts for sale).
questions.zh-question:
一家小型发动机生产商与一家割草机制造商签订合同，约定在未来三年内，以约定价格每月向后者供应5,000台特定型号的发动机。生产商向制造商发送了一份格式报价单，其中包含一项标准的“样板”赔偿条款，要求制造商就交易产生的损失对生产商进行赔偿。生产商的格式报价单中还包含一项诉讼时效条款，要求因发动机缺陷引起的索赔必须在交付后一年内提出。

随后，制造商使用一份格式订单订购发动机，该订单要求生产商就发动机缺陷引起的任何损失对制造商进行赔偿，并规定了因发动机引起的索赔的诉讼时效为三年。

两年后，制造商发现第一年交付的发动机中有20%存在缺陷，并对生产商提起诉讼，寻求赔偿。该司法管辖区已采纳《Uniform Commercial Code (UCC)》的补充条款（gap-filling provisions），其中包括一个默认为四年的诉讼时效。

制造商就缺陷发动机造成的损失对生产商提起的诉讼是否可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为根据镜像规则（mirror-image rule），只有当事人就所有条款达成合意（meeting of the minds），合同才可强制执行。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为生产商是要约的主导者（master of the offer），因此其格式报价单中的合同条款具有控制力。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为生产商在接受制造商的采购订单时，未对冲突的条款提出异议。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为《UCC》会用其四年的诉讼时效取代相互冲突的诉讼时效条款。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Formation of Contracts - Mutual assent

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：两家商人用表格互相加了冲突的违约救济和诉讼时效条款时，battle of the forms（格式之争）下这些冲突条款会不会被knockout rule（删除规则）踢掉，最后改用UCC默认规则。

三秒认题路径：

货物买卖 → 商人对商人 → 条款打架 → knockout rule → UCC补缺

核心法律规则

卖的是发动机，属于货物买卖，所以适用UCC，不是普通法的mirror-image rule（镜像规则）。在商人之间，接受函里新增或冲突的条款通常不会把整个合同搞没，knockout rule（删除规则）会把互相矛盾的条款一起删掉。删完以后，空出来的地方由UCC的gap-filling provisions（补缺规则）填上，所以争议会转回UCC默认的四年诉讼时效。

核心判例： UCC § 2-207 体系下的商人格式之争逻辑，冲突条款被删除后，由UCC默认规则补上空缺，故这里不是看谁表格先发。

思维导图

先看：这是最终合同解释问题，还是根本没合同？
1.有合同：双方已经就发动机买卖达成交易，争的是附加条款怎么处理。
2.适用UCC：货物买卖 + 商人之间 → 进入 battle of the forms（格式之争）。
3.冲突条款：
producer 说 1 年，manufacturer 说 3 年 → 互相打架，先一起删掉。
4.删完后的空位：
UCC gap-filling provisions（补缺规则） 自动补入 4年诉讼时效。
5.答案落点：
两年起诉没超时 → 制造商可以主张赔偿，选 D。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：谁先发报价、谁是offeror，就该由谁的表格控制全部条款。

但考试真正问的是：在UCC下，商人之间的冲突条款不是“谁赢谁输”，而是先被删除，再用默认规则补回去。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干里一边写 1年，一边写 3年，这两个时效条款正是冲突条款，商人之间会被删除后改用UCC默认4年诉讼时效（four-year statute of limitations），所以两年起诉仍然有效。

❌ 概念混淆 | 镜像规则误套

✕ A: 把货物买卖硬套成mirror-image rule，忘了UCC本来就不看完全一致。

❌ 法律适用 | 报价主控误判

✕ B: 看到先发报价就以为它包办一切，忽略了对方的冲突条款会被删除。

❌ 事实误判 | 未提异议偷换

✕ C: 把“没及时反对”当成关键事实，但本题走的是knockout rule，不是少数州的新条款自动并入规则。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看是不是货物买卖和商人交易，再专门盯“冲突条款删掉后谁补缺”。

考场速记

记住一句：battle of the forms（格式之争）里，冲突条款先删除，空位再由UCC补；如果你看到货物买卖、商人、表格打架，先想“删掉再补”，不要先想普通法镜像规则。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
An Impressionist painting valued at $400,000 was stolen from an art collector's home. The collector, who had insured the painting for $300,000 with an insurance company, promised to pay $25,000 to a full-time investigator for the insurance company if he effected the return of the painting to her in good condition. The insurance company's rules permit its investigators to accept and retain rewards from policyholders for the recovery of insured property. The investigator, by long and skillful detective work, recovered the picture and returned it undamaged to the collector.
If the collector refuses to pay the investigator anything, and he sues her for $25,000, what is the probable result under the prevailing modern rule?

choices.A: The collector wins, because the insurance company, the investigator's employer, had a preexisting duty to return the recovered painting to the collector.
choices.B: The collector wins, because the investigator owed the insurance company a preexisting duty to recover the picture if possible.
choices.C: The investigator wins, because the collector will benefit more from return of the $400,000 painting than from receiving the $300,000 policy proceeds.
choices.D: The investigator wins, because the preexisting duty rule does not apply if the promisee's (the investigator's) duty was owed to a third person.

questions.explanation:
Preexisting duty rule
Traditional common law rule Promise to perform, or performance of, preexisting duty does not constitute consideration
Modern exception Consideration exists if preexisting duty owed to third person (ie, nonparty to contract)

An enforceable contract must be supported by consideration—ie, a bargained-for exchange of promises or performance. Under the preexisting duty rule, the promise to perform, or the performance of, a legal duty that is already owed generally does not qualify as consideration. But under the modern exception to this rule, such a promise or performance is consideration if the preexisting duty is owed to a third person—ie, someone who is not a party to the contract in question.

Here, the art collector promised to pay the investigator $25,000 to find and return her stolen painting. Although the investigator owed his employer (the insurance company) a preexisting duty to recover that painting if possible, the insurance company was a third person with respect to the investigator's agreement with the collector (Choice B). This means that the traditional preexisting duty rule does not apply, and the investigator's recovery of the painting is sufficient consideration for the collector's promise. Therefore, the investigator will probably win.

(Choice A) Had the collector promised to pay the reward to the insurance company, then its preexisting duty under the insurance policy would make the collector's promise unenforceable. But since the collector promised to pay the investigator, the insurance company's preexisting duty is irrelevant.

(Choice C) The fact that the collector will benefit more from the return of the painting than from receiving the policy proceeds has no effect on the outcome of this dispute.

📌 Educational Objective

The promise to perform, or the performance of, a preexisting duty is not consideration unless the preexisting duty is owed to a third person (ie, someone who is not a party to the contract in question).

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 73 cmt. d (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (explaining that the performance of a preexisting contractual duty can be consideration if the duty is not owed to the promisor).
questions.zh-question:
一幅价值40万美元的印象派画作从一位艺术品收藏家的家中被盗。该收藏家曾为这幅画向一家保险公司投保了30万美元，并承诺如果该保险公司的一名全职调查员能将画作完好无损地归还给她，她将支付其2.5万美元。保险公司的规定允许其调查员接受并保留保单持有人为寻回受保财产而提供的奖赏。经过长期而巧妙的侦探工作，该调查员找回了画作并将其完好无损地归还给了收藏家。

如果收藏家拒绝向调查员支付任何款项，而调查员起诉她索要2.5万美元，那么根据现行的现代规则，可能的结果是什么？

zh-choices.A: 收藏家胜诉，因为调查员的雇主，即保险公司，有预先存在的义务将寻回的画作归还给收藏家。
zh-choices.B: 收藏家胜诉，因为调查员对保险公司负有预先存在的义务，即在可能的情况下寻回画作。
zh-choices.C: 调查员胜诉，因为归还价值40万美元的画作比获得30万美元的保险赔偿金能让收藏家获益更多。
zh-choices.D: 调查员胜诉，因为如果受约人（调查员）的义务是对第三方所负，则“已存义务规则”不适用。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Formation of Contracts - Consideration

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：先前义务规则（preexisting duty rule）在“义务是对第三人承担”时，为什么仍然能构成对价（consideration）。

三秒认题路径：

先前义务 → 对谁承担 → 第三人例外 → 有无对价 → 选赢方

核心法律规则

合同要可执行，必须有对价（consideration），也就是双方有交换。一般来说，已经负有的先前义务（preexisting duty），再去承诺履行，通常不算新的对价，考场意思：你只是把本来就该做的事再说一遍，不会换来新的合同。现代例外（modern exception）是：如果这份先前义务是对第三人（third person）负的，而不是对本案承诺人负的，那么履行它仍然可以构成对价。Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 73 cmt. d 正是把这条例外钉死了。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 73 cmt. d — 先前义务若是对第三人承担，履行它仍可作为对价。

思维导图

题干先问：被告为什么要付钱？因为侦探把被偷的画找回来了。
第一层：侦探是否本来就有义务？
有，但这份义务是对雇主保险公司（insurance company），不是对收藏家。
第二层：先前义务规则怎么卡？
卡死点：义务不是对本案承诺人，所以preexisting duty rule 不挡这里的对价。
结论：收藏家的 $25,000 承诺有对价 → 侦探可赢。
答案落点：选 D。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：侦探本来就“有义务找回失物”，所以不能再拿奖金。

但考试真正问的是：这份义务是对谁负的。题干里他对的是保险公司（insurance company），而收藏家是另一个人，所以第三人例外直接放行。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干关键事实是：侦探的先前义务是对保险公司，不是对收藏家；所以他完成找回失画时，仍给了收藏家新对价。

❌ 概念混淆 | 义务对象误判

✕ A: 把义务当成对收藏家，preexisting duty 才会卡住。

❌ 法律适用 | 第三人例外漏掉

✕ B: 只盯着雇主那层义务，漏看第三人例外。

❌ 事实误判 | 价值比较偷换

✕ C: “更划算”不等于有对价，benefit more 不是测试点。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定先前义务的受义务人，再判断是否落入第三人例外，别被画价差和情绪背景带跑。

考场速记

记忆口诀：先前义务不算对价，除非义务是对第三人。 这题直接记成一句：对第三人履行旧义务，也可能换来新合同。

reason.en: Indicates the promise that the plaintiff seeks to enforce.

reason.en: Directs the analysis to the modern exception for preexisting duties.

A.text: preexisting duty to return the recovered painting

reason.zh: 错误地适用雇主的义务来阻碍调查员的合同。

B.text: owed the insurance company a preexisting duty

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
A store owner mailed a signed order to a warehouse that read: "Please ship us 10,000 widgets at your current price." The warehouse manager received the order on January 7 and that same day mailed to the store owner a properly stamped, addressed, and signed letter stating that the order was accepted at the warehouse's current price of $10 per widget. On January 8, before receipt of the manager's letter, the store owner telephoned the manager and said, "I hereby revoke my order." The manager protested to no avail. The store owner received the manager's letter on January 9. Because of the store owner's January 8 telephone message, the warehouse never shipped the goods.
Under the relevant and prevailing rules, is there a contract between the store owner and the warehouse as of January 10?

choices.A: No, because the order was an offer that could be accepted only by shipping the goods, and the offer was effectively revoked before shipment.
choices.B: No, because the store owner never effectively agreed to the $10 price term.
choices.C: Yes, because the order was an offer that the warehouse effectively accepted before the store owner attempted to revoke it.
choices.D: Yes, because the order was, for a reasonable time, an irrevocable offer.

questions.explanation:
Contract negotiations by mail*
Offeror's
actions		 Offer
  • • Effective upon receipt
Revocation of offer
Offeree's
actions		 Acceptance
(mailbox rule)
  • • Effective upon dispatch
  • • Exceptions—effective upon receipt if:
    • ◦ improperly stamped/addressed
    • ◦ acceptance by mail unreasonable
    • ◦ rejection mailed before acceptance (first received is effective)
    • ◦ acceptance of option contract
    • ◦ offer states acceptance effective only upon receipt
Rejection/counteroffer
  • • Effective upon receipt
*Applicable under common law & UCC.

Contracts for the sale of goods are governed by Article 2 of the Uniform Commercial Code (UCC). Under the UCC, contract formation requires mutual assent (ie, offer and acceptance). Once an offer has been made, a contract will be formed if the offeree accepts the offer before it is revoked. Under the mailbox rule, acceptance by mail is:

  • • permitted if mail is a reasonable method of communicating acceptance—eg, when the offer was communicated by mail and
  • • effective upon dispatch—ie, when the acceptance is properly addressed and placed with the postal service with paid postage.

Here, the warehouse manager received the store owner's order for 10,000 widgets on January 7. Since that offer was communicated by mail, the warehouse manager could reasonably accept by mail or by shipping the goods (Choice A). Therefore, the warehouse manager effectively accepted the offer when he mailed a properly stamped and addressed acceptance letter on January 7—before the store owner tried to revoke the offer on January 8.

(Choice B) A sale-of-goods contract can be formed even if the price is to be set by just one of the parties. Therefore, the store owner did effectively agree to the $10 price when he ordered widgets at the manufacturer's "current price."

(Choice D) Certain types of offers are irrevocable, including firm offers—ie, a merchant's written and signed assurance that an offer will be held open for a specified period of time (not seen here).

📌 Educational Objective

Acceptance by mail is (1) permitted if mail is a reasonable method of communicating acceptance (eg, if the offer was communicated by mail) and (2) effective upon dispatch (ie, when the acceptance is properly addressed and placed with the postal service with paid postage).

📚 References
  • 17A Am. Jur. 2d Contracts § 98 (Am. Law Inst. 2019) (mailbox rule).
questions.zh-question:
一名商店店主向一个仓库邮寄了一份签名的订单，内容为：“请按你们现行的价格向我们发货10,000个小部件。” 仓库经理于1月7日收到该订单，并在当天向该店主邮寄了一封贴好邮票、写明地址并签名的信函，声明该订单已按仓库现行的每个10美元的价格被接受。1月8日，在收到仓库经理的信函之前，店主致电经理说：“我在此撤销我的订单。” 经理提出抗议，但无济于事。店主于1月9日收到了经理的信函。由于店主1月8日的电话通知，仓库从未发货。

根据相关且通行的规则，截至1月10日，店主与仓库之间是否存在合同？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为该订单是一项只能通过发货行为来接受的要约，而该要约在发货前已被有效撤销。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为店主从未有效同意每件10美元的价格条款。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为该订单是一项要约，仓库在店主试图撤销该要约之前已经有效地接受了它。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为该订单在一段合理的时间内是一项不可撤销的要约。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Formation of Contracts - Formation of Contracts

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：邮件发出的承诺是否已经按投邮规则（mailbox rule）成立，所以要看“先投邮接受，还是后电话撤销”。

三秒认题路径：

要约已到手 → 邮件去接受 → 投邮即生效 → 先于撤销 → 有合同

核心法律规则

买卖货物合同（sale of goods contract）受UCC第2编管，先有要约（offer），再看承诺（acceptance）有没有在撤销前作出。这里的关键是投邮规则（mailbox rule）：如果用邮件是合理的沟通方式，承诺在正确贴邮、写明地址并投递邮局时就生效，考场意思：不用等对方真的收到。

所以，电话撤销如果晚于承诺投邮，撤销就追不上；题目问的是“到January 10有没有合同”，答案只看 January 7 那封接受信是否已经把合同锁住。

这题不需要去找firm offer，因为题干没有“商人书面保证保留要约”的事实。

核心判例： 邮件承诺规则（mailbox rule）——接受在适当投邮时生效，所以先投邮的承诺先把合同成立。

思维导图

先看：仓库经理的回信有没有在撤销前生效？
1.要约已通过邮件送达，邮件本来就是合理的接受方式。
2.接受信在 January 7 已正确贴邮、写址、投递。
卡死点：承诺（acceptance）在投邮那一刻就生效，不等 January 9 收到。
3.January 8 的电话撤销来晚了，已经撤不掉已成立的合同。
结论：January 10 时，双方已经有合同，选 C。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然仓库后来没有发货，是不是说明合同没成，或者一定要等商品真的寄出才算接受。
但考试真正问的是：邮件接受是否先于撤销已经完成，所以看的是投邮时点，不是后来有没有发货。
司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干里仓库经理在 January 7 就把接受信正确投邮了，先于 January 8 的电话撤销，所以合同已经成立。

❌ 法律适用 | 发货当成生效

✕ A: 把shipping the goods当成唯一接受方式了。

❌ 概念混淆 | 价格条款误读

✕ B: 把“current price”误当成没同意价格。

❌ 事实误判 | 试图套固化要约

✕ D: 题干没有firm offer那种书面保留要约。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓“邮件接受是否已投邮”，再看撤销有没有赶上。

考场速记

记住：承诺（acceptance）走邮件时，通常是“正确投邮即生效”，不是“对方收到才生效”；所以先投邮、后撤销，合同就已经锁定了。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
A developer, needing a water well on one of his projects, met several times about the matter with a well driller. Subsequently, the driller sent the developer an unsigned typewritten form captioned "WELL DRILLING PROPOSAL" and stating various terms the two had discussed but not agreed upon, including a "proposed price of $5,000." The form concluded, "This proposal will not become a contract until signed by you [the developer] and then returned to and signed by me [the driller]."
The developer signed the form and returned it to the driller, who neglected to sign it but promptly began drilling the well at the proposed site on the developer's project. After drilling for two days, the driller told the developer during one of the developer's daily visits that he would not finish unless the developer would agree to pay twice the price recited in the written proposal. The developer refused, the driller quit, and the developer hired a substitute driller to drill the well to completion for a price of $7,500.
In an action by the developer against the driller for damages, which of the following is the probable decision?

choices.A: The developer wins, because his signing of the driller's form constituted an acceptance of an offer by the driller.
choices.B: The developer wins, because the driller's commencement of performance constituted an acceptance by the driller of an offer by the developer and an implied promise by the driller to complete the well.
choices.C: The driller wins, because he never signed the proposal as required by its terms.
choices.D: The driller wins, because his commencement of performance merely prevented the developer from revoking his offer, made on a form supplied by the driller, and did not obligate the driller to complete the well.

questions.explanation:
Bilateral v. Unilateral contracts
Offer Effect of beginning performance
Unilateral Invites acceptance by performance of act
  • Creates option contract that prevents offeror from revoking offer
  • Offeree is not bound to complete performance
Bilateral Invites acceptance by return promise
  • Serves as acceptance of offer
  • Offeree is bound to complete performance

An offer is a communication that gives the recipient the power to conclude a contract by accepting the offer in an appropriate manner, without the need for any further action by the other party. Here, the driller's initial proposal was not an offer because the developer could not complete the deal by signing the proposal and returning it to the driller, who also needed to sign (Choice A). But when the developer signed the proposal and returned it to the driller, he was making an offer on the terms described in the proposal.

The driller could have accepted by signing the proposal as required by its terms, thereby making a return promise to complete the well. However, a bilateral offer that requires a return promise to accept can be accepted with a return promise or by starting performance (eg, beginning the well drilling) (Choice C). Starting performance operates as an implied promise to render complete performance (eg, complete the well). Therefore, the driller's failure to complete the well was a breach, and the developer will win in his action for damages.

(Choice D) An offer to form a unilateral contract arises when one party promises to do something in exchange for an act of the other party—eg, pay a monetary reward in exchange for finding a lost dog (not seen here). Once performance has begun, the offer is irrevocable for a reasonable period of time to allow for complete performance. However, the recipient is not bound to complete performance.

📌 Educational Objective

An offer is a communication that gives the recipient the power to conclude a contract by acceptance without further action by the other party. A bilateral offer that requires a return promise to accept can be accepted either with a return promise or by starting performance, which operates as an implied promise to render complete performance.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 24 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (offer defined).
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 62 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (effect of beginning performance).
questions.zh-question:
一个开发商，因其一个项目需要一口水井，就此事与一个钻井工多次会面。随后，钻井工向开发商发送了一份未签署的打印表格，标题为“水井钻探提案”，其中陈述了双方讨论过但未达成一致的各项条款，包括“报价5000美元”。表格最后写道：“本提案在由您[开发商]签署并返还给我[钻井工]签署后，方能成为一份合同。”

开发商签署了该表格并将其返还给钻井工，钻井工忽略了签署，但立即在开发商项目的拟定地点开始钻井。钻井两天后，在开发商的一次日常探访中，钻井工告诉开发商，除非开发商同意支付书面提案中所述价格的两倍，否则他不会完工。开发商拒绝了，钻井工随即停工，开发商雇佣了另一名钻井工以7500美元的价格将水井钻探完成。

在开发商对钻井工提起的损害赔偿诉讼中，以下哪项是可能的判决？

zh-choices.A: 开发商胜诉，因为他签署钻井工的表格构成了对钻井工要约的承诺。
zh-choices.B: 开发商胜诉，因为钻井工开始履行构成了钻井工对开发商要约的承诺，并默示了钻井工将完成水井的允诺。
zh-choices.C: 钻井工胜诉，因为他从未按照提案条款的要求签署该提案。
zh-choices.D: 钻井工胜诉，因为他开始履行仅仅是阻止了开发商撤销其在钻井工提供的表格上所作的要约，并未使钻井工负有完成水井的义务。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Formation of Contracts - Mutual assent

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：双务要约（bilateral offer）能否通过开始履行（beginning performance）构成承诺，并把对方锁进继续履行义务。

三秒认题路径：

先看要约类型 → 再看怎么承诺 → 开始履行了吗 → 是否承诺成立 → 谁违约

核心法律规则

要约（offer） 是把“把合同做成”的权力交给对方，所以你要先看题干有没有让受领人一招就能完成合同。双务要约（bilateral offer） 的考场意思：对方用“回信承诺”就能成交，但也可以用开始履行来表示同意。开始履行（beginning performance） 一旦出现，通常就会带出一个必须完成的默示承诺（implied promise）来把剩余工作做完。单务合同（unilateral contract） 则是“做成动作才算接受”，开始履行通常只是让要约先别撤回，不等于对方已经被绑定要做完。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 62 - 开始履行在双务要约里通常等于接受，并附带完成履行的默示承诺。

思维导图

题干先问：这是 双务要约（bilateral offer） 还是 单务要约（unilateral offer）？
先判定：表格写明“signed by you and then returned and signed by me”，说明要的是回签承诺，不是做完动作才算成交。
双务路径：回签是承诺；开始履行（beginning performance） 也可当作承诺。
事实钉子：打井人拿到签字后马上开工，等于用行动接受对方的要约。
卡死点：开始履行不只是“保住要约不撤回”，而是把自己锁进“要完成”的义务里。
结论：停工拒绝完工 = 违约 → 开发商可索赔。
答案落点：所以不是选“没签字就没合同”，而是选“已通过开始履行接受，要完成未完成部分”。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：对方没在表上签字，所以合同还没成。

但考试真正问的是：开发商签回去以后，打井人已经用开工这种方式接受了要约，后面不能只做一半就抽身。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的工程有没有先开始」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干签回后即开工，说明打井人用开始履行接受了开发商的要约，并附带完成工程的默示承诺，所以中途停工构成违约。

❌ 概念混淆 | 回签误当承诺

✕ A: 把开发商回签当成对原表的承诺，但原表要的是双方都签，顺序已经变成他在下要约。

❌ 法律适用 | 单务规则套错

✕ C: 看到never signed就以为无合同，但这题不是单务悬赏，而是可用开始履行接受的双务要约。

❌ 事实误判 | 只记住撤回效力

✕ D: 只盯着prevented revocation，漏掉了开始履行还会把对方绑上完成义务。

这题建议用什么方法？

先分清双务还是单务，再看开始履行是在“保住要约”还是“直接接受并锁定完工”。

考场速记

记住一句：双务要约（bilateral offer） 里，开始履行常常就是承诺；单务要约（unilateral offer） 里，开始履行通常只是防撤回，不等于必须做完。

口诀：In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely 这个口诀是中间上诉专用；本题别乱套，真正要记的是“回签要约 + 开工接受 = 绑住完工义务”。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
A lawn service company agreed in writing to purchase from a supplier all of its requirements for lawn care products during the next calendar year. In the writing, the supplier agreed to fulfill those requirements and to give the company a 10% discount off its published prices, but it reserved the right to increase the published prices during the year. After the parties had performed under the agreement for three months, the supplier notified the company that it would no longer give the company the 10% discount off the published prices.
Does the company have a viable claim against the supplier for breach of contract?

choices.A: No, because the absence of a minimum quantity term rendered the company's promise illusory.
choices.B: No, because the supplier could, and did, revoke its offer with respect to future deliveries.
choices.C: Yes, because part performance of the agreement by both parties made it enforceable for the full year.
choices.D: Yes, because the company's agreement to buy all of its lawn care products from the supplier made the agreement enforceable.

questions.explanation:
Contract terms for sale of goods (Article 2 UCC)
Terms Requirements Effect if missing
Goods to be sold Must be reasonably identified No contract
Quantity Must be certain or able to be made certain by reference to objective facts
Price N/A Gap-filler: reasonable price at time of delivery
Time of delivery Gap-filler: reasonable time
UCC = Uniform Commercial Code.

Article 2 of the Uniform Commercial Code (UCC) governs contracts for the sale of goods. Under the UCC, an offer becomes irrevocable once it is accepted. The resulting contract must contain definite terms that:

  • reasonably identify the goods to be sold and
  • specify a quantity of goods to be sold that is certain or capable of being made certain by reference to objective facts.

The quantity term is sufficiently definite in a requirements contract—ie, a contract for the sale of as many goods as the buyer needs during a specified period—because the buyer's actual requirements can be determined objectively.

Here, the lawn service company and the supplier entered into a requirements contract wherein the lawn service company agreed to buy all of its lawn care products from the supplier for one year at a 10% discount.* Although this contract did not contain a certain quantity, the terms were sufficiently definite because the company's actual requirements could be determined objectively. Therefore, the contract was enforceable for its entire one-year term, and the supplier breached the contract by refusing to give the discount three months later (Choice B).

*The supplier reserved the right to increase its published prices—not to revoke the 10% discount on those prices.

(Choice A) A promise is illusory, and therefore unenforceable, if the promisor has discretion whether to perform at all (eg, X promises to buy such goods as X wishes to order from Y). But here, the absence of a minimum quantity term does not render the company's promise illusory since it is still required to buy (and the supplier is still required to sell) all lawn care products it actually needs.

(Choice C) A contract whose terms would otherwise be too vague to be enforced may become enforceable based on part performance if the parties' subsequent acts supply the needed clarification of the terms (not needed here).

📌 Educational Objective

Contracts for the sale of goods must specify a quantity of goods to be sold that is certain or capable of being made certain by reference to objective facts—eg, the buyer's actual requirements for a product can be used to determine quantity under a requirements contract.

📚 References
  • U.C.C. § 2-306 cmt. 2 (Am. Law Inst. & Unif. Law Comm'n 2020) (explaining that the quantity term is sufficiently definite in output and requirements contracts).
questions.zh-question:
一家草坪服务公司书面同意，在下一个日历年度内，向一家供应商采购其所需的全部草坪护理产品。在该书面文件中，供应商同意满足这些需求，并给予该公司其公布价格的10%折扣，但保留了在该年度内提高公布价格的权利。双方根据协议履行了三个月后，供应商通知该公司，将不再给予其公布价格的10%折扣。

该公司是否可以向供应商提出可行的违约索赔？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为缺乏最低数量条款使得该公司的承诺虚幻不实。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为供应商可以，并且事实上已经撤销了其关于未来交付的要约。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为双方对协议的部分履行使其在整个年度内均可强制执行。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为该公司同意向该供应商购买其全部草坪护理产品，这使得该协议可强制执行。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Formation of Contracts - Indefiniteness & absence of terms

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：UCC货物买卖合同里，数量条款（quantity term）只要能用客观事实确定，哪怕是requirements contract，也通常不是无效合同。

三秒认题路径：

货物买卖 → requirements → 数量可定 → 终局有效 → 可起诉违约

核心法律规则

这题看的是UCC Article 2（统一商法典第二编）下，货物买卖合同是否足够确定。数量条款（quantity term）不用写死具体数字，只要能靠客观事实算出来就行，最典型就是requirements contract（需求合同）。

所谓 requirements contract，考场意思：买方承诺买自己“实际需要的全部”，所以数量不是拍脑袋，而是看买方真实需求。只要买方必须向卖方买，卖方也必须供货，这份合同就能成立并被执行。

核心判例： U.C.C. § 2-306 cmt. 2 — 需求合同的数量可以由买方实际需求客观确定，所以不会因为没写固定数字就当然无效。

思维导图

先看是不是货物买卖下的数量不确定问题？
事实触发： 写的是“买我全年所有 lawn care products”
规则关卡： 数量能不能用客观事实确定？
YES： requirements contract，买方实际需要量可算
NO： 纯空话、想买多少就买多少，才会出问题
本题卡死点：
没写最低数量 ≠ 取消买卖义务；买方仍必须买“实际需要的全部”
结论： 合同有效，供应商三个月后单方改成不打折，构成违约

考点陷阱

你可能会想：没写最低数量，是不是买方承诺太空，所以合同无效。

但考试真正问的是：买方是不是仍然被绑定去买“自己实际需要的全部”；只要能按客观事实算数量，就不是空 promise。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干写的是全年all of its requirements，这正是可按客观需求确定数量的合同，所以合同有效，供应商不能中途撤回折扣。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把需求合同误看成no minimum quantity就当然空约。

❌ 法律适用 | 撤回对象误判

✕ B: 把“改折扣”偷换成撤回要约，忽略它已经成了合同。

❌ 事实误判 | 履行补正误判

✕ C: 题干不需要靠part performance补漏洞，合同本来就够确定。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看是不是 UCC 货物合同，再盯数量是否能由需求客观确定。

考场速记

记住：requirements contract（需求合同）不怕没写具体数字，只怕买方真的能随便决定买不买。
口诀：买方要“全量需求”，不是“想买就买”；能客观算出来，合同就站得住。

A.text: absence of a minimum quantity term

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
A toy collector purchased 10 antique toys over several years and had had them restored by an expert in toy restoration. On June 1, the collector sent an 11th antique toy to the expert with a signed note that read: "Here is another toy for you to restore. As with all prior jobs, I will pay $500 for the work, but no more." On June 4, after receipt of the collector's June 1 note and the toy, the expert began restoring the toy. On June 6, the collector unexpectedly died. On June 7, unaware of the collector's death, the expert sent the collector a note that stated that the restoration work had begun on June 4. The following day, the expert learned of the collector's death.
Does a contract exist that binds the expert and the collector's estate?

choices.A: No, because the collector died before the expert sent the June 7 note.
choices.B: No, because the offer lapsed when the collector died.
choices.C: Yes, because the expert sent the June 7 note before learning of the collector's death.
choices.D: Yes, because the offer was accepted before the collector's death.

questions.explanation:
Bilateral v. Unilateral contracts
Offer Effect of beginning performance
Unilateral Invites acceptance by performance of act
  • Creates option contract that prevents offeror from revoking offer
  • Offeree is not bound to complete performance
Bilateral Invites acceptance by return promise
  • Serves as acceptance of offer
  • Offeree is bound to complete performance

Contract formation requires mutual assent (ie, offer and acceptance). An offer that invites acceptance by return promise—or an offer that does not specify a manner of acceptance—can be accepted by either (1) promising to perform the requested act or (2) performing the requested act. Acceptance by performance is effective as soon as the offeree begins to perform.* However, the offeror is not obligated to perform until receiving notice of the acceptance. And if the offeror dies prior to acceptance, the offer will terminate by law.

Here, the toy collector offered to pay the restoration expert $500 in exchange for the restoration of an antique toy. The expert accepted that offer by beginning to restore the toy on June 4—before the collector's death on June 6. Therefore, a contract exists that binds the expert and the collector's estate.

*Unlike in a bilateral contract, in a unilateral contract, only the offeree's complete performance constitutes acceptance.

(Choices A, B & C) The offer would have terminated by law if the collector had died before acceptance. But the expert began to perform (acceptance) before the collector's death. Therefore, a binding contract existed regardless of whether the collector died before the expert sent the note or the expert sent the note before learning of the collector's death.

📌 Educational Objective

Unless an offer specifies a manner of performance, it can be accepted by (1) promising to perform the requested act or (2) performing the requested act. Acceptance by performance is effective as soon as the offeree begins to perform, but the offeror is not obligated to perform until receiving notice of the acceptance.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 32 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (explaining that an offer generally invites acceptance by either performing or promising to perform).
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 62 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (explaining that the beginning of performance is an acceptance that obligates the offeree to complete the performance).
questions.zh-question:
一名玩具收藏家在几年间购买了10件古董玩具，并请一位玩具修复专家对它们进行了修复。6月1日，该收藏家将第11件古董玩具寄给这位专家，并附上一张亲笔签名的便条，上面写着：“这是另一件给您修复的玩具。与之前所有工作一样，我将为此工作支付500美元，不能再多。” 6月4日，专家在收到收藏家6月1日的便条和玩具后，开始修复该玩具。6月6日，收藏家意外去世。6月7日，专家在不知道收藏家已去世的情况下，给收藏家寄去一张便条，称修复工作已于6月4日开始。第二天，专家得知了收藏家的死讯。

是否存在一份对专家和收藏家遗产具有约束力的合同？

zh-choices.A: 不存在，因为收藏家在专家发送6月7日的便条之前就已去世。
zh-choices.B: 不存在，因为要约因收藏家去世而失效。
zh-choices.C: 存在，因为专家在得知收藏家去世之前发送了6月7日的便条。
zh-choices.D: 存在，因为要约在收藏家去世前已被接受。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Formation of Contracts - Mutual assent

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：要约（offer）能否被 开始履行（beginning performance） 视为承诺，以及在 要约人死亡（death of offeror） 前是否已经完成承诺。

三秒认题路径：

要约看方式 → 可用履行承诺 → 先开始履行 → 死亡在后 → 合同成立

核心法律规则

如果要约没有指定只能用某一种方式接受，通常可以用 承诺（promise） 或 履行（performance） 来接受。对 单务合同（unilateral contract） 来说，开始履行（beginning performance） 就已经构成承诺，考试里你要抓的是“先开始做了没有”。

一旦受要约人已经开始履行，合同就先锁住了；要约人之后死亡，通常不能把已经成立的合同倒回去。只有在死亡发生于承诺之前，要约才会因法律而终止。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 62 - 开始履行本身就是承诺，所以本题在 June 4 就已经把要约锁住了。

思维导图

June 1
要约：“我付你 500 美元修复”
没限定只能用哪种接受方式
June 4
专家开始修复
这一步就是 承诺（acceptance）
June 6
收藏家死亡
但此时合同已经被 June 4 锁住
June 7
事后发通知只是补充说明
不是决定合同成立的关键
关卡：死亡前是否已经承诺？
YES： June 4 已开始履行 → 承诺完成 → 合同成立
NO： 若先死后承诺 → 要约依法终止
卡死点：不是看 June 7 的通知先后，而是看 June 4 是否已经开始履行

考点陷阱

你可能会想：June 7 note 先发出，所以合同应该等到通知那一刻才成立。

但考试真正问的是：专家在 June 4 已经开始履行，承诺（acceptance） 那时就完成了，后面的通知只是告诉对方“我已经接了”。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干 June 4 开始修复 这一动作已经构成承诺，发生在 June 6 死亡之前，所以合同已成立并约束遗产。

❌ 事实误判 | 通知时点偷换

✕ A: 把 June 7 note 当成成立时点了。

❌ 法律适用 | 死亡终止误套

✕ B: 只盯着死亡规则，漏掉死亡前已承诺的关键事实。

❌ 概念混淆 | 通知必要性误判

✕ C: 以为没先通知就没合同，before learning 不是成立门槛。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定接受方式，再看承诺发生时间；只要开始履行早于死亡，答案就直接落在“合同成立”。

考场速记

记住这句：要约没限方式时，开始履行就是承诺；先履行，后死亡，合同照样成立。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
The owner of the manuscript of a widely acclaimed novel offered in writing to sell it to a university at a specified price. When contacted by phone by the university about the offer, the owner gratuitously stated that she would give the university a month to weigh her offer. Three weeks later, the university decided to accept the offer but learned from a reliable third party that a museum had purchased the manuscript from the owner. The university delivered its acceptance of the offer to the owner the next day. When the owner refused to deliver the manuscript to the university, the university filed a breach of contract lawsuit against the owner.
Which of the following is the owner's best defense to this lawsuit?

choices.A: Impracticability.
choices.B: Parol evidence rule.
choices.C: Revocation.
choices.D: Statute of frauds.

questions.explanation:
Termination of offer before acceptance
Offeror's revocation
  • Offeror communicates revocation directly to offeree
  • Offeree learns information from reliable source that reasonably indicates offer was revoked (eg, house sold to another buyer)
Offeree's rejection
  • Offeree communicates rejection directly to offeror
  • Offeree's counteroffer serves as rejection & new offer*
Lapse
  • Time period specified in offer expires
  • After reasonable time if no time period specified in offer
By law
  • Either party dies or is adjudicated insane
  • Subject matter of offer is destroyed or becomes illegal
*Counteroffer does not terminate offer if offeree manifests intent to take offer under advisement.

An offer can generally be revoked by the offeror at any time prior to acceptance. The offeror must generally communicate the revocation of the offer to the offeree for the revocation to be effective. However, if the offeree acquires reliable information that the offeror has taken definite action inconsistent with the offer, the offer is automatically revoked (i.e., a constructive revocation occurs).

Here, the owner offered to sell the university her manuscript and promised to give the university a month to weigh her offer. But before the month expired, the owner sold it to a museum. Although the owner did not communicate a revocation of her offer to the university, the university learned of the manuscript's sale from a reliable third party prior to accepting the offer. Since that sale was inconsistent with the owner's offer to sell the manuscript to the university, the owner's best defense is that the offer was constructively revoked before the university accepted it.

(Choice A) The defense of impracticability requires that an unanticipated or extraordinary event make it impracticable for a party to perform its contractual obligations. Here, the owner's offer was constructively revoked prior to acceptance, so the owner is not a party to a contract and has no contractual obligations.

(Choice B) The parol evidence rule applies to agreements reached before or contemporaneously with the execution of a written contract. But there was no written contract here. Further, the owner's oral statement related to how long she would let the university contemplate her offer—not to an agreement with the university as to a term of the contract itself.

(Choice D) The statute of frauds prevents the enforcement of certain contracts that are not in writing. Here, there was no contract—only an offer that was constructively revoked before acceptance.

📌 Educational Objective

An offeror must generally communicate the revocation of an offer to the offeree for the revocation to be effective. However, if the offeree acquires reliable information that the offeror has taken definite action inconsistent with the offer, the offer is automatically revoked.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 43 (Am. L. Inst. 1981) (providing that an offeree's power of acceptance is terminated when the offeror takes definite action inconsistent with an intention to enter into the proposed contract and the offeree acquires reliable information to that effect).
questions.zh-question:
一份广受好评的小说手稿的所有者书面提出以特定价格将其出售给一所大学。当大学通过电话联系所有者询问该要约时，所有者无偿表示将给大学一个月时间考虑她的要约。三周后，大学决定接受该要约，但从可靠的第三方得知一家博物馆已经从所有者那里购买了该手稿。大学次日向所有者发出了对该要约的接受。当所有者拒绝向大学交付手稿时，大学对所有者提起了违约诉讼。
以下哪项是所有者对该诉讼的最佳抗辩？

zh-choices.A: Impracticability（不可行性）。
zh-choices.B: Parol evidence rule（口头证据规则）。
zh-choices.C: Revocation（撤销）。
zh-choices.D: Statute of frauds（反欺诈法）。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Formation of Contracts - Mutual assent

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：要约人在接受前把标的卖给第三人，算不算对原要约的构成性撤回（constructive revocation）。

三秒认题路径：

先有要约 → 未到接受 → 卖给别人 → 可靠消息 → 视为撤回

核心法律规则

要约（offer）一般可以在接受前被撤回；通常要把撤回直接通知给受要约人（offeree），考场意思：让对方知道你不打算继续卖了。

但如果受要约人从可靠来源得知，要约人已经作出与要约 inconsistent 的明确行为，比如把标的卖给别人，受要约人的接受权就会自动终止，这叫构成性撤回（constructive revocation）。

核心判例：Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 43——要约人作出与缔约意图不一致的明确行为，且受要约人获得可靠信息时，接受权就消失。

思维导图

先看：受要约人的接受权还在吗？
1.有书面要约，原本可接受。
2.接受前，要约人把 manuscript 卖给 museum。
3.受要约人从 可靠第三方（reliable source） 得知。
卡死点：不是“有没有亲口通知”，而是是否已知对方做了与要约相反的事。
结论：接受权已终止，后来的接受太晚，答案选 C。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：对方没亲口说撤回，所以要约还在。

但考试真正问的是：受要约人是否已经从可靠来源知道，要约人做了和要约相反的事。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干的关键是：大学在接受前，已从可靠第三方得知 manuscript 被卖给 museum，这就是构成性撤回，所以合同没成立。

❌ 法律适用 | 性质套错

✕ A: 把它当成履行不能了，但这里连合同都还没成立。

❌ 概念混淆 | 证据规则误套

✕ B: 误把口头承诺当成 parol evidence 问题了。

❌ 事实误判 | 先有合同前提

✕ D: 这里没有已成立合同，statute of frauds 进场太早。

这题建议用什么方法？

先盯接受权是否还活着，再看有没有可靠消息触发构成性撤回。

考场速记

记住一句：接受前卖给别人 + 可靠消息，通常就等于撤回；MBE 看到这个组合，先想 revocation，别先乱找合同抗辩。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
In January, a garden center contacted a farmer who owned a greenhouse about growing seedlings for sale in the spring. The garden center promised in writing to buy, at a fixed price, all of the seedlings that the farmer raised in his greenhouse. As a consequence, a few days later the farmer purchased containers and seeds and hired a worker to prepare the containers, plant the seeds, and tend to the seedlings. Later that week, he emailed the garden center to tell it he had taken these actions. Just prior to the delivery of any seedlings, the garden center notified the farmer that it would not purchase any of the seedlings. The farmer sold the seedlings at a price far below the price set by the garden center.
The farmer filed a breach of contract action to recover damages.
Will the farmer likely succeed?

choices.A: No, because the garden center did not receive consideration for its promise to buy the farmer's output.
choices.B: No, because the garden center revoked its offer before it was accepted by the farmer.
choices.C: Yes, because the doctrine of promissory estoppel made the offer irrevocable.
choices.D: Yes, because the farmer accepted the garden center's offer by beginning performance.

questions.explanation:
Bilateral v. Unilateral contracts

Offer
Acceptance
Effect
Bilateral
Invites acceptance
by return promise
Returns promise or
begins performance
+ notice
Contract formed
Unilateral
Invites acceptance
by performance
Completes performance
+ notice (if required)
Contract formed

Contract formation requires mutual assent, which occurs upon acceptance of an offer to enter a contract. Unless an offer specifies that it can only be accepted by performance (ie, unilateral contract), it can be accepted by promising or beginning performance. If acceptance is made by beginning performance, the offeree must notify the offeror within a reasonable time that performance has begun. Failure to do so will result in a lapse of the offer.

Here, the garden center promised to buy all the seedlings raised by the farmer. Since the farmer began to raise the seedlings—eg, by purchasing containers and seeds and by hiring a worker to tend the seedlings—the farmer accepted the garden center's offer by beginning performance. And since the farmer notified the garden center of this acceptance within a reasonable time ("later that week"), the garden center could not subsequently revoke its offer and refuse to buy the seedlings (Choice B). Therefore, the farmer will likely succeed.

(Choice A) The garden center did receive consideration because its promise induced the farmer's reciprocal commitment to produce and sell the seedlings.

(Choice C) Under the doctrine of promissory estoppel, an offer may become irrevocable if the offeree reasonably and detrimentally relies on it before acceptance. But this doctrine does not apply here since acceptance occurred, and a contract was formed, when the farmer began to raise the seedlings and notified the garden center.

📌 Educational Objective

Unless an offer specifies that it can only be accepted by performance, it can be accepted by promising or beginning performance. An offeree who accepts by beginning performance must notify the offeror within a reasonable time that performance has begun.
questions.zh-question:
一月，一家园艺中心联系了一位拥有温室的农场主，商议为春季销售培育幼苗。该园艺中心书面承诺，将以固定价格购买该农场主在其温室中培育的所有幼苗。因此，几天后，该农场主购买了容器和种子，并雇佣了一名工人来准备容器、播种和照料幼苗。在那周晚些时候，他通过电子邮件告知园艺中心他已采取了这些行动。就在任何幼苗交付之前，园艺中心通知农场主，他们将不会购买任何幼苗。农场主以远低于园艺中心设定价格的价格出售了这些幼苗。

农场主提起了违约诉讼以寻求损害赔偿。

该农场主可能会胜诉吗？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为园艺中心为其购买农场主产出的承诺没有收到对价。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为园艺中心在农场主接受之前撤销了其要约。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为 promissory estoppel 原则使得该要约不可撤销。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为农场主通过开始履行接受了园艺中心的要约。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Formation of Contracts - Mutual assent

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：普通要约如果没有限定只能用履行接受，受要约人可以通过开始履行（beginning performance）来接受；一旦接受成立，发出方一般不能再撤回。

三秒认题路径：

要约买输出 → 开始履行 → 及时通知 → 接受成立 → 不能撤回

核心法律规则

合同成立看的是双方同意（mutual assent），也就是受要约人有没有按要约要求把接受送出去。除非要约明确说“只能靠履行接受”，否则它既可以用承诺（promise）接受，也可以用开始履行（beginning performance）接受。

如果是通过开始履行来接受，受要约人还要在合理时间内通知要约人：performance has begun。本题里农民买容器、买种子、雇工照料，已经是在开始履行；后来又在“那周晚些时候”发邮件通知，所以接受已经完成。

核心判例：本题对应的规则就是普通的双务/单务接受区分：未限定只能履行时，开始履行 + 合理通知 = 合同成立，之后撤回来不及。

思维导图

要约是否限定“只能通过履行接受”?
否：通常可用承诺（promise）或开始履行（beginning performance）接受。
农民是否已开始履行？
买容器、买种子、雇工照料 → 这不是准备聊天，是在把合同做起来。
是否在合理时间内通知？
是：后来那周就发邮件通知 → 接受完成，发出方不能再单方撤回。
结论：选 D。
是：若明确只可履行接受，才转向“完成履行”规则。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：花了钱、雇了人，好像只是依赖了对方承诺，所以应该走promissory estoppel。

但考试真正问的是：这里不是先看信赖救济，而是先看接受（acceptance）有没有已经成立；一旦开始履行并及时通知，合同已经形成。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干里农民已通过购买容器和种子、雇工照料开始履行，再加上及时邮件通知，所以接受成立，花园中心之后撤回太晚了。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把输出合同硬扯成consideration缺失，但双务承诺本来就有对价。

❌ 事实误判 | 提前撤回误判

✕ B: 说先撤回就赢，是漏看了农民已经开始履行并通知。

❌ 法律适用 | 信赖救济误套

✕ C: 把promissory estoppel当主轴，但这里已经有合同成立，不靠它补洞。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看要约有没有限定接受方式，再抓“开始履行 + 及时通知”这两个成立点。

考场速记

记忆口诀：未限履行接受时，开始履行（beginning performance）就能接受；记得“做了、并且通知了”，合同就先成立。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
On July 18, a shovel manufacturer received an order for the purchase of 500 snow shovels from a wholesaler. The wholesaler had mailed the purchase order on July 15. The order required shipment of the shovels no earlier than September 15 and no later than October 15. Typed conspicuously across the front of the order form was the following: "Wholesaler reserves the right to cancel this order at any time before September 1." The manufacturer's mailed response, "We accept your order," was received by the wholesaler on July 21.
As of July 22, which of the following is an accurate statement as to whether a contract was formed?

choices.A: A contract was formed, but prior to September 1 it was an option contract terminable only at the will of the wholesaler.
choices.B: A contract was formed, but prior to September 1 it was terminable at the will of either party.
choices.C: No contract was formed, because of the wholesaler's reservation of the right to cancel.
choices.D: No contract was formed, because the wholesaler's order was only a revocable offer.

questions.explanation:
Consideration problems that prevent contract formation
Gift No bargained-for exchange
Token consideration No inducement to bargain if performance entirely devoid of value
Sham consideration No legal detriment & no inducement to bargain if recited performance not intended to be completed
Preexisting duty / past consideration No legal detriment if performance already owed or completed
Illusory promise No legal detriment if apparent promise imposes no obligation

Under the UCC, which governs contracts for the sale of goods, contract formation requires:

  • mutual assent – an offer and acceptance and
  • valuable consideration – a bargained-for exchange of promises or performance.

Once a contract is formed, it cannot be terminated unilaterally (Choice B). But if either party's promise is illusory because it imposes no obligation on that party, then there is no consideration and no contract.

Here, the wholesaler sent a purchase order to the shovel manufacturer and received a mailed acceptance on July 21. But the purchase order imposed no obligation on the wholesaler because it reserved the right to cancel at any time before September 1. As a result, the wholesaler's promise to purchase shovels was illusory. Due to this lack of consideration, no contract was formed as of July 22.

(Choice A) An option is a type of contract in which one party promises to hold a separate offer open for a specified time in return for consideration. Here, however, there was no promise to hold the offer open for any amount of time. And if an option contract had formed, it would not be terminable at the will of either party.

(Choice D) Offers are revocable prior to acceptance (with a few exceptions), so the revocability of an offer does not prevent contract formation. But since the wholesaler reserved the right to cancel (ie, revoke) at any time before September 1, its illusory promise to purchase shovels prevented contract formation.

📌 Educational Objective

An illusory promise is one that imposes no obligation on the promising party and therefore fails to provide the consideration needed for contract formation.

UCC = Uniform Commercial Code
📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 77 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (explaining that an apparent promise is not consideration if it makes performance entirely optional).

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Formation of Contracts - Formation of Contracts

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：买方把随时取消（right to cancel）保留到合同形成前，导致承诺变成不具约束力的虚假承诺（illusory promise），所以没有合同。

三秒认题路径：

保留取消权 → 承诺不受拘束 → 没有对价 → 没有合同 → 选 C

核心法律规则

UCC下，货物买卖合同（sale of goods contract）要成立，既要有合意（mutual assent），也要有对价（consideration），也就是双方都得真的被绑定。

如果一方表面上像在承诺，实际上却给自己留了随时撤回或取消的自由（illusory promise），考试上就等于“我说了，但我不用做”，这种话不算对价。

所以本题里，买方写明在9月1日前任何时候都能取消（at any time before September 1），这让它的购买承诺没有法律拘束力，合同还没形成。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 77 - 只要表面承诺把履行变成完全可选，就不是对价。

思维导图

先看：买方的“承诺”有没有真的绑住自己？
事实触发：订单写着 may cancel at any time before September 1
法律后果：买方保留随时取消权 → 承诺变成 illusory promise
结果1：没有对价（consideration）
结果2：没有有效合同形成
卡死点：不是“能不能撤销要约”，而是“这句话有没有给出真正的法律义务”。
答案落点：所以到 7月22日，选 C

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然卖方已经回信接受了，那合同就成了，后面最多只是“可不可以取消”的问题。

但考试真正问的是：买方那句“我随时能取消”让它根本没有把自己绑住，所以连合同门槛都没跨过去。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「表面上已经收到了接受信」这种外观。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干 reserved the right to cancel at any time before September 1，让买方承诺没有约束力，所以没有对价（consideration），也就没有合同。

❌ 概念混淆 | 选项身份错认

✕ A: 把这当成option contract，但题干根本没有“对价换保留要约”的承诺。

❌ 法律适用 | 终局前可解错位

✕ B: 以为先成约后再单方终止，但这里卡在形成前，买方从一开始就没被绑住。

❌ 事实误判 | 把要约当取消权

✕ D: 把买方的revocable offer说成一般要约可撤回，忽略了这份订单本身就是买方的承诺问题。

这题建议用什么方法？

先盯住“承诺有没有绑定自己”，再判断对价，别被“已经接受”这层外观带跑。

考场速记

记住一句：一方保留随时取消权，通常就是illusory promise，对价没了，合同也没了。

看到“保留撤回 / 取消 / 任意决定是否履行”，先问：这是不是把义务变成了“想做就做”？如果是，直接往“无对价、无合同”走。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
A construction company contracted with a regional distributor to construct for $500,000 a warehouse and a driveway at highway level. Shortly after commencing work on the driveway, which required for the specified level some excavation and removal of surface material, the construction company unexpectedly encountered a large mass of solid rock.
The construction company informed the distributor (accurately) that because of the rock, the driveway as specified would cost at least $20,000 more than figured and demanded for that reason a total contract price of $520,000. Since the distributor was expecting warehousing customers immediately after the agreed completion date, he signed a writing promising to pay the additional $20,000. Following timely completion of the warehouse and driveway, which conformed to the contract in all respects, the distributor refused to pay the construction company more than $500,000.
What is the maximum amount to which the construction company is entitled?

choices.A: $500,000, because the distributor's promise to pay the additional $20,000 was exacted under duress.
choices.B: $500,000, because there was no consideration for the distributor's promise to pay the additional $20,000.
choices.C: $520,000, because the modification was fair and was made in the light of circumstances not anticipated by the parties when the original contract was made.
choices.D: $520,000, provided that the reasonable value of the construction company's total performance was that much or more.

questions.explanation:
Modifying existing contracts
Governing law Requirements
Common law Traditional view
  • Parties' agreement
  • New consideration
Modern view
  • Parties' agreement
  • New consideration unless modification is fair & equitable due to unanticipated circumstances
UCC
  • Parties' agreement
  • Good faith (ie, honesty & observance of reasonable commercial standards of fair dealing)
  • New consideration not required
UCC = Uniform Commercial Code.

At common law, contract modifications generally must be supported by new consideration to be enforceable. This requires both parties to alter their duties in some way. However, modifications are enforceable without new consideration if the modification:

  • rests on circumstances not anticipated by the parties when the contract was made* and
  • is fair and equitable in light of those circumstances.

Here, the construction company and the distributor originally agreed on a contract price of $500,000. During excavations, the construction company unexpectedly encountered a large mass of solid rock. This unanticipated circumstance was going to increase construction costs by at least $20,000, so increasing the contract price by $20,000 was fair and equitable. Therefore, the modification was effective even though the construction company provided no new consideration, and the construction company is entitled to $520,000 (Choice B).

*Circumstances prompting the modification must have been unanticipated by the parties, but they need not have been completely unforeseeable.

(Choice A) A contract modification is voidable if it was induced by duress—ie, physical force or improper threat. But here, even though the distributor was expecting warehousing customers immediately after the agreed completion date, there is no indication that his promise to pay the $20,000 was exacted under duress.

(Choice D) Contract law does not require the value of a party's performance to be equal to or greater than the contract price. Therefore, the reasonable value of the construction company's performance need not be $520,000 or more for the distributor to owe it.

📌 Educational Objective

Under common law, contract modifications generally must be supported by new consideration—ie, each party must alter its duties in some way. But new consideration is not required if the modification is fair and equitable in light of unanticipated circumstances.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 89 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (explaining that modification of a contract without new consideration is binding if it is fair and equitable in view of unanticipated circumstances).

一家建筑公司与一家区域经销商签订合同，以500,000美元的价格建造一个仓库和一条与公路齐平的车道。在开始修建车道后不久——该工程为达到指定高度需要进行一些挖掘和地表材料的清除——建筑公司意外地遇到了一大块坚硬的岩石。

建筑公司（准确地）告知经销商，由于这块岩石，按规定修建车道的成本将比预算至少高出20,000美元，并因此要求合同总价为520,000美元。由于经销商预计在约定的完工日期后立即有仓储客户入住，他签署了一份书面文件，承诺支付额外的20,000美元。在仓库和车道按时完工且各方面均符合合同后，经销商拒绝向建筑公司支付超过500,000美元的款项。

建筑公司有权获得的最大金额是多少？

zh-choices.A: 500,000美元，因为经销商支付额外20,000美元的承诺是在胁迫下作出的。
zh-choices.B: 500,000美元，因为经销商支付额外20,000美元的承诺没有对价。
zh-choices.C: 520,000美元，因为该变更是公平的，并且是根据双方在订立原始合同时未预料到的情况作出的。
zh-choices.D: 520,000美元，前提是建筑公司全部履约的合理价值等于或超过该金额。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Formation of Contracts - Formation of Contracts

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：普通法下合同变更是否需要新对价，还是可以因为双方未预见的突发情况而直接生效。

三秒认题路径：

原合同500k → 挖出岩层 → 加价20k → 未预见情况 → 变更有效

核心法律规则

只抓这条规则

普通法下，合同变更（modification）一般要有新的 对价（consideration），也就是双方都得让步或改变义务。Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 89 说得很直白：如果变更是因为双方当时没有预见（unanticipated）的情况，而且在这些情况下面显得公平合理（fair and equitable），那即使没有新对价，也能成立。考试里你只要看：这是不是“突然冒出来的成本/风险”，而不是一方临时坐地起价。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 89 - 这条规则直接锁定：未预见到的岩层导致成本飙升时，加价变更可以有效。

思维导图

1. 原始合同
约定总价 $500,000，先看这是普通法变更题。
2. 突发事实
施工中挖到 solid rock，成本至少再多 $20,000。
3. 法律关卡
未预见情况 + 公平合理 → 新对价（new consideration） 不再是死门槛。
4. 误区排除
不是 duress，因为题目只有催促交付，没有不当威胁。
5. 错误思路
别把“没有新对价”直接等于无效；这里有 Restatement § 89 例外。
6. 结论
变更有效，承包商可拿 $520,000。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然原合同是 $500,000，后来多要 $20,000，那一定缺少新对价，所以只能拿回原价。

但考试真正问的是：这次加价是不是因为双方当时没想到的岩层，导致成本真的上升；如果是，普通法允许把变更做成有效。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干的 solid rock 属于双方原先没预见到的突发成本，且多收 $20,000 在此情形下公平合理，所以变更有效，承包商可拿 $520,000。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把催促付款当成 duress，题干根本没不当威胁。

❌ 法律适用 | 对价门槛误套

✕ B: 死扣“没新对价”，漏掉了未预见情况这个例外。

❌ 事实误判 | 价值要价偷换

✕ D: 把争点偷换成“工作值不值 $520,000”，题目问的是变更能不能成立。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看是不是普通法变更题，再问有没有未预见情况把“新对价”这道门打开。

考场速记

普通法改约先看 新对价（new consideration），但遇到未预见的突发成本且加价公平合理时，Restatement § 89 会把变更救活。记住一句：“意外成本 + 公平加价 = 变更有效。”

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
A woman obtained a bid of $10,000 to tear down her old building and another bid of $90,000 to replace it with a new structure in which she planned to operate a sporting goods store. Having only limited cash available, the woman asked a local businessman for a $100,000 loan. After reviewing the plans for the project, the businessman in a signed writing promised to lend the woman $100,000 secured by a mortgage on the property and repayable over 10 years in equal monthly installments at 10% annual interest. The woman promptly accepted the demolition bid and the old building was removed, but the businessman thereafter refused to make the loan. Despite diligent efforts, the woman was unable to obtain a loan from any other source.
Does the woman have a cause of action against the businessman?

choices.A: No, because the woman's inability to obtain a loan from any other source demonstrated that the project lacked the financial soundness that was a constructive condition to the businessman's performance.
choices.B: No, because there was no bargained-for exchange of consideration for the businessman's promise to make the loan.
choices.C: Yes, because by having the building demolished, she accepted the businessman's offer to make the loan.
choices.D: Yes, because her reliance on the businessman's promise was substantial, reasonable, and foreseeable.

questions.explanation:
Promissory estoppel claim
Did promisor reasonably expect to induce reliance on promise?
Yes
↓
Did enforcing party reasonably rely on promise?
Yes
↓
Did reliance cause enforcing party substantial detriment?
Yes
↓
Is enforcement of promise necessary to avoid injustice?
No → Deny claim
Yes
↓
Uphold claim

The equitable doctrine of promissory estoppel allows a party to recover damages stemming from another's failure to perform a promise when there is no valid contract (as seen here). Recovery under promissory estoppel is warranted if:

  • the promisor reasonably expected to induce reliance on the promise
  • the enforcing party reasonably relied on the promise
  • reliance on the promise caused the enforcing party to suffer substantial detriment and
  • injustice can only be avoided by enforcing the promise.

Here, the woman had not accepted the businessman's loan offer, so there was no valid contract between the two. However, the woman substantially, reasonably, and foreseeably relied on the businessman's promise of a loan by accepting the demolition bid. As a result, she can assert a cause of action for promissory estoppel against the businessman (and will likely prevail).

(Choice A) A constructive condition is one that is not expressly stated in a contract but is implied by law. Financial soundness of a project is not a constructive condition to performance of a party's promise to make a loan.

(Choice B) There was no bargained-for exchange of consideration for the businessman's promise, which would be required to recover under a breach-of-contract theory. But consideration is not needed to recover under a claim of promissory estoppel.

(Choice C) There are no facts indicating that the businessman authorized the woman to accept his offer to make a loan by demolishing the building. Therefore, this is not a basis for a cause of action against the businessman.

📌 Educational Objective

Promissory estoppel can be used to enforce a promise when no valid contract has been formed if (1) the promisor reasonably expected to induce reliance on the promise, (2) the promise did induce such reliance, (3) that reliance caused the other party substantial detriment, and (4) injustice can only be avoided by enforcing the promise.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 90 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (promissory estoppel).
questions.zh-question:
一名女性获得了一份拆除其旧建筑的1万美元报价，以及一份以新建筑取而代之的9万美元报价，她计划在新建筑中经营一家体育用品店。由于手头现金有限，该女性向一位当地商人请求10万美元的贷款。在审查了该项目计划后，该商人在一份签署的书面文件中承诺，向该女性出借10万美元，以该房产的抵押权作为担保，偿还期为10年，以等额月度分期付款方式偿还，年利率为10%。该女性立即接受了拆除报价，旧建筑被拆除，但此后该商人拒绝提供贷款。尽管该女性尽力努力，但仍无法从任何其他来源获得贷款。

该女性对该商人是否拥有诉因？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为该女性无法从任何其他来源获得贷款，表明该项目缺乏财务稳健性，而财务稳健性是该商人履行的推定条件。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为对于该商人提供贷款的承诺，不存在经协商的对价交换。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为通过拆除建筑物，她接受了该商人提供贷款的要约。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为她对该商人承诺的信赖是重大的、合理的且可预见的。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Formation of Contracts - Promises Binding Without Consideration

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：允诺禁反言（promissory estoppel）能不能在没有对价（consideration）时，把一份本来没成立的贷款承诺救活。

三秒认题路径：

没对价 → 有承诺 → 有信赖 → 有损害 → 可否救济

核心法律规则

这条规则怎么用

当没有有效合同，但允诺禁反言（promissory estoppel）成立时，法院可以为了避免不公而执行承诺。要看四件事：承诺人是否应当预见对方会信赖，信赖（reliance）是否真的发生，信赖是否造成重大损害（substantial detriment），以及不执行承诺是否会带来不公。

这题里， businessman 先签字承诺放贷，女人随即拆掉旧楼，属于典型的可预见、合理、实际发生的信赖。考场上你不用先找对价；这里的关键是：她已经按这句话去行动了，所以可以用 promissory estoppel 追责。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 90 锁定本题：没有合同也可能因可预见信赖而强制履行承诺。

思维导图

先看：这是一份已经成立的合同吗？
否：没有完成“要约 + 承诺 + 对价”的普通合同路径。
再问：能不能靠 promissory estoppel 补上？
1. 承诺人应当预见会诱发信赖
2. 对方确实合理信赖
3. 信赖带来重大损害
卡死点：这里不是“有没有对价”，而是“拆楼后还能不能救济”。
4. 为避免不公，需要执行承诺
结论：满足 → 选 D

考点陷阱

你可能会想：她没有正式接受贷款，所以只是没谈成的合同。
但考试真正问的是：有没有一种不靠对价也能救她的路径，也就是 允诺禁反言（promissory estoppel）。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

命题人还会拿“项目不够稳”“她自己冒险”来带偏你，但这题没有把财务稳健设成放贷人的构成条件。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干 she promptly accepted the demolition bid，说明她已按放贷承诺去拆楼，属于可预见、合理且造成损害的信赖，所以可用 promissory estoppel 救济。

❌ 事实误判 | 财务条件偷换

✕ A: 把 financial soundness 硬塞成前提，题干根本没这道门槛。

❌ 法律适用 | 对价规则错搬

✕ B: 只盯着 consideration，忘了这里问的是信赖救济，不是违约之诉。

❌ 概念混淆 | 接受方式误认

✕ C: 把拆楼当成接受贷款要约，但题干没说他允许她用这种方式接受。

这题建议用什么方法？

先分清普通合同和信赖救济，再看有没有“预见信赖 + 实际损害”。

考场速记

记住一句：允诺禁反言（promissory estoppel）不是拿对价赢，是拿“我已经按你这句话行动了”赢。看到签字承诺后立刻去拆楼、搬家、开工这类动作，先想信赖救济，再想合同。
